name: Făgăraș Land
summary: Făgăraș Land is a depression and a historical region in Transylvania, located along the middle course of the Olt river, with its center in the medieval Făgăraș fortress. In 1876, the territory of Făgăraș Land was organized into Făgăraș county, the administrative unit preceding the interwar Făgăraș county. Through Law no. 5 of September 6, 1950, after the establishment of the Romanian People's Republic, the interwar counties were abolished, and Făgăraș Land was incorporated into the newly created Sibiu Region; this being abolished in 1952, the Făgăraș territory was included in the Stalin Region, which, in 1960, was renamed the Brașov Region. In 1966, with the administrative-territorial reorganization of the Socialist Republic of Romania, Făgăraș Land was divided between the current Brașov and Sibiu counties.

sources.title: Ethnographic zones – Museum of the Romanian Peasant
sources.excerpt: Located in the contact area of the Făgăraș and Perșani Mountains, Lotru, and the Hârtibaciu Plateau. Occupies the center-west of Brașov county and the south-east of Sibiu county. Representative villages: Sâmbăta de Sus, Lisa.
